{{DISPLAYTITLE:Shimizu ''L''-function}}{{More citations needed|date=November 2025}}

In [[mathematics]], the '''Shimizu ''L''-function''', introduced by Hideo Shimizu in 1963,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Shimizu |first=Hideo |date=January 1963 |title=On Discontinuous Groups Operating on the Product of the Upper Half Planes |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1970201?origin=crossref |journal=The Annals of Mathematics |volume=77 |issue=1 |pages=33 |doi=10.2307/1970201|url-access=subscription }}</ref> is a [[Dirichlet series]] associated to a [[totally real number field|totally real]] [[algebraic number field]]. {{harvs|txt | last1=Atiyah | first1=Michael Francis | author1-link=Michael Atiyah | last2=Donnelly | first2=H. | last3=Singer | first3=I. M. | author3-link=Isadore Singer | title=Eta invariants, signature defects of cusps, and values of L-functions | url=https://dx.doi.org/10.2307/2006957 | doi=10.2307/2006957 |mr=707164 | year=1983 | journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |series=Second Series | issn=0003-486X | volume=118 | issue=1 | pages=131–177}}<ref>{{Citation |last1=Atiyah |first1=Michael Francis |title=Eta invariants, signature defects of cusps, and values of L-functions |journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |volume=118 |issue=1 |pages=131–177 |year=1983 |series=Second Series |doi=10.2307/2006957 |issn=0003-486X |jstor=2006957 |mr=707164 |last2=Donnelly |first2=H. |last3=Singer |first3=I. M. |author1-link=Michael Atiyah}}</ref> defined the [[signature defect]] of the boundary of a [[manifold]] as the [[eta invariant]], the value as ''s''=0 of their eta function, and used this to show that Hirzebruch's signature defect of a cusp of a [[Hilbert modular surface]] can be expressed in terms of the value at ''s''=0 or 1 of a Shimizu L-function.

==Definition==

Suppose that ''K'' is a totally real algebraic number field, ''M'' is a lattice in the field, and ''V'' is a subgroup of maximal rank of the group of totally positive units preserving the lattice. The Shimizu L-series is given by
:<math>L(M,V,s) = \sum_{\mu\in \{M-0\}/V} \frac{\operatorname{sign} N(\mu)}{|N(\mu)|^s}</math>
